status: bounded apparatus outline only; not a task or instruction
public_apparatus_facts: Use the same uniform incompressible Newtonian charged-fluid slab and reduced electromagnetic units as r3, with rho=m*n0, p^2=n0*q^2/m, current J=q*n0*v, fixed neutralizing background and full linear Maxwell and transverse momentum response.

Each stationary face carries an optically inert massless spring and Newtonian dashpot in series. Fluid slip is the extension rate plus dashpot velocity; common traction is k(T)*e=kappa*v_d. There is no additional surface response or internal relaxation.

The spring is a locally equilibrated elastic material. Measured isothermal force data give k(T)=k0*[1+(T-T0)/(2*T0)] for .9*T0<=T<=1.1*T0, where T0 is a known positive absolute reference temperature. Its heat capacity per area at fixed extension is a known positive constant C0. The dashpot coefficient is independent of temperature. Known alpha=kappa/rho and tau=kappa/k0 specify the contact at T0.

An ideal thermostat holds the whole front contact, including elastic element and dashpot, at T0. Its calibrated signed heat removal per area is the measured signal. Heat in the bulk fluid and rear contact is collected separately. There is no detector delay, extra work channel or temperature feedback at the stated order; equilibrium background is subtracted.

Normally incident light has incoming electric field Re[E0*exp(-i*frequency*t)] at the front face with real E0. No light enters from the rear. Take periodic stationarity before the weak-field limit at leading quadratic heat order. This clock defines the two harmonic quadratures.

Normalize whole-contact heat by incident mean power E0^2/2. Return its mean, twice its mean product with cos(2*frequency*t), or twice its mean product with sin(2*frequency*t). Outputs are dimensionless and quadratures are signed.

Frequency has inverse-time units, d has length, alpha has length/time and tau has time; k0 has traction/length units and C0 has energy/(area*temperature) units. All controls and material data except p are known.

Retain the unrestricted documented fit/predict interface and an ordinary None fit stub if a package is authorized. No thermodynamic correction formula or numerical algorithm restriction belongs in public prose.
calibration_intent: Exactly the unchanged nonzero finite-memory mean settings and fixed .0002 instrument sigma; no data generation or new interface was performed here.
private_reference_scope: Collocation electromagnetic/fluid fields and real series-contact dynamics, with whole-contact first-law heat from the thermodynamic internal energy. No final phasor heat factor is inserted into this reference.
